public_rationale: The claim covers every declaration of AGI that Marcus himself has seen. No public record lists those declarations, so the word 'every' cannot be checked. Whether a definition is 'redefining downwards' also depends on which definition is taken as the standard. The contract treats that as a judgement call, not a measurement. The packet has two example declarations, and both are context only. A Futurism report (available 2024-12-09) quotes OpenAI staffer Vahid Kazemi. He said AGI had been achieved and described current systems as 'better than most humans at most tasks', not 'better than any human at any task'. A Noema essay by Agüera y Arcas and Norvig (2023-10-10) says AGI 'means many different things to different people'. It argues that the most important parts of AGI have already been achieved by current large language models. Whether either definition is weaker than the earlier ones depends on the baseline chosen. Neither item can test a universal claim about what Marcus personally read. So the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: The evidence does not show which declarations Marcus saw. It also does not show whether he saw these two.
Only two example declarations are in the packet. They are context only and cannot stand for the whole set.
There is no agreed baseline definition of AGI, so 'downwards' cannot be measured objectively.
Futurism gives the date of the Kazemi post only as December 2024. The article was available on 2024-12-09.
